newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ousted Cambodian premier due in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Cambodian premier due in Philippines.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh plans to fly to the Philippines soon as part of efforts to win support in the region, foreign ministry officials said on Friday.

"He is part of the solution and part of the problem, so you have to listen to him...so that we may be able to determine the form of solution that is acceptable to all," Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon told reporters.
Ranariddh, forced to flee Cambodia after a coup by arch rival Second Prime Minister Hun Sen early in July, could arrive as early as Sunday, officials said.
The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) has called for a ceasfire by supporters of the two prime ministers.
The group -- which comprises Brunei, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Laos, Burma and Singapore -- had planned to accept Cambodia as a member last month.
But it was forced to postpone entry after the crisis in Cambodia erupted when Hun Sen staged the coup.
Ranariddh, who has already visited Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia, may meet President Fidel Ramos, Siazon said.
Ranariddh's father, King Norodom Sihanouk, has refused to endorse Hun Sen.
